$comment: The Ver. 7.0.14 duel board, recovered from pixels rather than from prose.
PROVENANCE. Every earlier note in this project flagged the board as the one
significant second-hand claim left, triangulated from Smogon's description and an
official point count. It is no longer triangulated. The graph below was extracted
programmatically from the board asset published at
https://github.com/gurish165/Pokemon_Duel (Assets/game_board.png, 2048x1152): white
pixels were thresholded, node discs recovered by morphological erosion, and an edge
recorded wherever the straight corridor between two node centres was continuously
white and contained no third node. That procedure returned 28 nodes and 34 edges
with no hand-placed edges, which is what makes it evidence rather than a redrawing.
WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. The asset is a fan reimplementation's board art,
not a first-party diagram, so it is one witness and not an authority. It is believed
because five independent facts fall out of it that were never fed into it:
1. 28 nodes total, matching the official 'fields made up of 26 points (and two
goals)'.
2. 34 edges, matching the figure this project had already recorded.
3. A 7x5 outer ring and a 3x3 inner ring with the corners of both squares joined,
matching Smogon's prose description exactly.
4. Both goals come out at degree 2 and all four entry corners at degree 3, with no
node outside 2..3 - the degree facts the surround rules depend on.
5. The graph is invariant under a 180 degree rotation and is NOT mirror symmetric,
which is a claim Smogon makes and which nothing about drawing a pretty board
would produce by accident. The asymmetry is real and load-bearing: see
goalSideDiagonals below.
A SECOND IMAGE IN THE SAME REPOSITORY DISAGREES AND IS REJECTED.
README_Images/Pokemon_Duel_Game_Board.jpg draws a 7x4 outer ring, 26 nodes, 28 edges,
no corner diagonals, and degree-2 entry corners. It was analysed by the same script.
It is rejected because it contradicts the official 26-plus-2 point count outright,
contradicts Smogon's '7x5', and would leave entry corners and goals indistinguishable
by degree. It reads as a simplified redrawing.
RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY, STATED PLAINLY. Nobody on this project has seen a running copy
of the game. If a first-party board render ever surfaces and disagrees, correcting
this file is a JSON edit: the engine reads the graph as data and derives every
relation - reachability, step distance, connected components, surround arity - from
it, so no code changes.
RULING 1 IS NOW CONFIRMED, NOT GUESSED. docs/RULES.md ruling 1 asks whether the two
goal-side diagonals meet the ring node beside the goal or the next one out, and ships
'adjacentToGoal' at medium confidence. The extracted edges are r4c2--i2c1 and
r0c4--i0c1; r4c2 and r0c4 are each immediately adjacent to their goal. The shipped
default was right. The loader still honours GOAL_SIDE_DIAGONAL_ATTACHMENT so the
constant stays load-bearing and the alternative reading stays one token away.
COORDINATES are normalised to the unit square for the renderer only. No rule reads
them. They are snapped to exact lattice fractions so the data file is exactly
180-degree symmetric even though the source pixels were a few units off.
NAMING. Outer ring nodes are r{row}c{col} on a 5-row by 7-column perimeter, row 0
being player 1's back row and row 4 player 0's. Inner ring nodes are i{row}c{col} on
a 3x3 grid with no centre.
orientation: portrait; player 0 defends row 4, player 1 defends row 0

$comment: One diagonal per goal, and they sit on OPPOSITE sides of their goals. That is not
a transcription slip: it is what makes the board 180-degree symmetric rather than
mirrored, and it is the single most surprising thing the pixel extraction found.
Under 'adjacentToGoal' the outer endpoint touches the goal's neighbour; under
'oneNodeOut' it steps one further along the ring. Both readings preserve 28 nodes,
34 edges and goal degree 2, which is exactly why prose could not settle it.
